Chapter Ten: Living with Expectation.
As we reach the end of these stories, a fresh question rises up—what does it really mean to live with expectation?
Imagine waking up each morning and actually believing that miracles are still possible. That hope isn’t some naïve idea, but something you genuinely need.
Let me tell you about a teacher—someone who’d faced more than her share of letdowns. Instead of bracing herself for the next disappointment, she tried a different approach. She opened her hands to each new day, actually looking for signs of hope, and noticing those small moments when good things quietly showed up.
Some days, the miracles were easy to spot—like finally breaking through with a student who’d struggled for months, or receiving an answer to a long-held prayer. And on other days? The miracles were quieter—a simple laugh, or a feeling of peace right in the middle of chaos.
Think, too, of a retiree staring down an uncertain future. Instead of letting fear take over, he chose to live with expectation. Suddenly, opportunities popped up where he used to see only obstacles. He started trusting that something good could still happen, no matter his age or circumstances.
And you know what? Over time, not only did his outlook shift, but so did his whole experience of life. The real miracle wasn’t just in what happened to him—but in how he learned to see the world with new eyes.
Most of us don’t even notice how quickly we slide into resignation—how easily we stop expecting good things. But these stories of miracles? They invite us to live differently. To wake up with hope. To keep our eyes open for the unexpected. To believe that, somehow, even the stones in our path can be moved.
Living with expectation doesn’t mean pretending everything’s easy or denying the hard stuff. It’s about choosing hope anyway. Trusting. Keeping our hearts open to the good, even on the tough days.
The journey isn’t always smooth. The obstacles don’t always disappear the way we want. But the invitation is still there—every single day—to live with open eyes, open hands, and an open heart.
